title: Neural networks are clean
dot:
digraph{rankdir=TB;graph[bgcolor="#FAFBFC", fontname="Helvetica", nodesep=0.4, ranksep=0.5, pad=0.3];node[fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=11, style="rounded,filled", shape=box, margin="0.15,0.1"];edge[color="#4A5568", arrowsize=0.7, fontsize=10];title[label="Neural Networks
Are Already Clean", fillcolor="#1A202C", fontcolor="#FFFFFF", fontsize=16, shape=box, penwidth=0];thesis[label="Core claim:
Networks use ONE learning principle —
generalization, not generalization
+ superposition", fillcolor="#E6F2FF", color="#2B6CB0", penwidth=2];old_fear[label="Old fear (misread evidence):
Superposition — unrelated concepts
packed arbitrarily into neurons.
Required untangling via SAEs first.", fillcolor="#FFE5E5", color="#C53030"];reality[label="Actual motif:
Recursive generalization — neurons
branch into related, adjacent territory.
Study the network directly.", fillcolor="#D9F7E1", color="#2F855A"];{rank=same;old_fear;reality}thesis->old_fear[label="The field believed…", fontcolor="#C53030"];thesis->reality[label="Close study shows…", fontcolor="#2F855A"];canon[label="The canonical evidence that failed:

4e:55 “cat + car” neuron was really
shared V-shape (cat faces, car fronts,
flames, fox snouts). The “car hidden in
dogs” circuit was shared pose.", fillcolor="#FFF8E1", color="#B7791F"];old_fear->canon[style=dashed, color="#C53030"];five[label="Why neurons appear polysemantic:

1. Bad tools
2. Bad explanations
3. Bad architecture / learning
4. Recursive generalization ★ (usual)
5. Superposition ★ (rarely if ever)", fillcolor="#F3E8FF", color="#6B46C1"];canon->five;evidence[label="Evidence:

• InceptionV1 last layer: ~0% → 99–100%
  interpretable with modern architecture
• Qwen3-32B: ~90% of neurons
  have one main job
• Crushing layers → coarser neurons,
  never arbitrary packing
• SAEs mostly rediscover neurons", fillcolor="#E6F2FF", color="#2B6CB0"];five->evidence;four[label="The optimistic argument:

1. One learning principle →
   no blocker to direct science
2. Ordinary science works well
3. Understanding compounds
4. Interpretability may be far more
tractable than feared", fillcolor="#FFE5E5", color="#C53030"];evidence->four;}
